title: The Loop, One Arrow at a Time

scenes.visual: Title card: The Loop, One Arrow at a Time.

scenes.tts: Every cell in the cluster now has proneural factor. So what picks one?
scenes.visual: The competent cluster from chapter two. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Every cell in the cluster now has proneural factor. So what picks one?

scenes.tts: The cells signal to each other through Notch. The signal says, not you.
scenes.visual: Speech bubbles between neighbours: not you.
scenes.narration: The cells signal to each other through Notch. The signal says, not you.

scenes.tts: Delta is a protein in the membrane of one cell. It binds Notch on the cell it touches, and pulls.
scenes.visual: Two touching cells. Delta, a ball on a stick, meets Notch, a crescent, and tugs.
scenes.narration: Delta is a protein in the membrane of one cell. It binds Notch on the cell it touches, and pulls.

scenes.tts: Two cuts then free the inner part of Notch. That part enters the nucleus.
scenes.visual: Two scissors marks on Notch; the inner piece moves into the nucleus.
scenes.narration: Two cuts then free the inner part of Notch. That part enters the nucleus.

scenes.tts: There, with a DNA-binding protein called C S L, it turns on target genes.
scenes.caption: There, with a DNA-binding protein called CSL, it turns on target genes.
scenes.visual: In the nucleus the inner piece sits on a protein labelled CSL on DNA. Small label: Suppressor of Hairless in the fly.
scenes.narration: There, with a DNA-binding protein called CSL, it turns on target genes.

scenes.tts: In a proneural cluster, the targets that matter are the Enhancer of split genes.
scenes.caption: In a proneural cluster, the targets that matter are the Enhancer of split, or E(spl), genes.
scenes.visual: Gene label: E(spl), Enhancer of split.
scenes.narration: In a proneural cluster, the targets that matter are the Enhancer of split, or E(spl), genes.

scenes.tts: They make repressors that switch proneural genes off.
scenes.visual: An E(spl) repressor sits on a proneural gene, which dims.
scenes.narration: They make repressors that switch proneural genes off.

scenes.tts: Proneural factors do two things in return. They raise their own expression.
scenes.visual: A proneural factor points back at its own gene, which brightens.
scenes.narration: Proneural factors do two things in return. They raise their own expression.

scenes.tts: And, in the standard model, they raise Delta.
scenes.visual: The proneural factor points to Delta, which grows on the membrane. Label: standard model.
scenes.narration: And, in the standard model, they raise Delta.

scenes.tts: Now follow two neighbours, A and B, one step at a time.
scenes.visual: Two cells labelled A and B side by side, with a two-column table below: cell A, cell B.
scenes.narration: Now follow two neighbours, A and B, one step at a time.

scenes.tts: Step one. A has a little more Delta. B gets more Notch activity, so B makes more repressor.
scenes.visual: Table row 1 fills: A sends more not you; B more Notch activity, more E(spl).
scenes.narration: Step one. A has a little more Delta. B gets more Notch activity, so B makes more repressor.

scenes.tts: Step two. B is repressed. It has less proneural factor, so it makes less Delta.
scenes.visual: Table row 2 fills: B less proneural factor, less Delta. B dims.
scenes.narration: Step two. B is repressed. It has less proneural factor, so it makes less Delta.

scenes.tts: Step three. The signal coming back to A is weaker. A makes less repressor, and more proneural factor.
scenes.visual: Table row 3 fills: A less Notch activity, less E(spl), more proneural factor.
scenes.narration: Step three. The signal coming back to A is weaker. A makes less repressor, and more proneural factor.

scenes.tts: So A makes more Delta. The returning signal pushes A's Delta up again, in the direction of its original lead. Whether the lead ends up bigger depends on how steep the loop is. That comes next.
scenes.visual: A return arrow nudges A's Delta up again, in the direction of the original lead; a question mark over whether it ends bigger or smaller. Label: direction, not yet size.
scenes.narration: So A makes more Delta. The returning signal pushes A's Delta up again, in the direction of its original lead. Whether the lead ends up bigger depends on how steep the loop is. That comes next.

scenes.tts: Each cell inhibits its neighbour. So A inhibits the cell that inhibits A.
scenes.visual: Two curved inhibition arrows, A to B and B to A, forming a circle.
scenes.narration: Each cell inhibits its neighbour. So A inhibits the cell that inhibits A.

scenes.tts: Two inhibitions in a row act as positive feedback. This is a switch-making arrangement.
scenes.visual: The two minus signs combine into one plus sign. Link card: signaling circuits.
scenes.narration: Two inhibitions in a row act as positive feedback. This is a switch-making arrangement.

scenes.tts: If the loop is steep enough, noise gives one cell a lead, and the loop magnifies it. In this ideal pair, which cell wins is chance.
scenes.visual: A coin flip icon over the pair; either A or B lights up. Label: steep loop.
scenes.narration: If the loop is steep enough, noise gives one cell a lead, and the loop magnifies it. In this ideal pair, which cell wins is chance.

scenes.tts: Predict. Neither cell has any Notch. What happens to the pair?
scenes.visual: Prompt card: No Notch in either cell. The two cells with their crescents removed.
scenes.narration: Predict. Neither cell has any Notch. What happens to the pair?

scenes.visual: Hold on the prompt. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: Neither cell can be told, not you. Both keep proneural genes on, and both become neural.
scenes.visual: Reveal: both cells glow and are labelled neural.
scenes.narration: Neither cell can be told, not you. Both keep proneural genes on, and both become neural.

scenes.tts: Too many neural cells. Fly geneticists call this the neurogenic phenotype, here in miniature.
scenes.visual: Label: neurogenic phenotype, too much neural tissue, in miniature.
scenes.narration: Too many neural cells. Fly geneticists call this the neurogenic phenotype, here in miniature.

scenes.tts: Now the reverse. Switch Notch on in both cells, whatever Delta they receive.
scenes.visual: Both crescents glow constantly.
scenes.narration: Now the reverse. Switch Notch on in both cells, whatever Delta they receive.

scenes.tts: Repressor stays high in both. Neither becomes neural, and the cluster gives no precursor.
scenes.visual: Both cells dim and are labelled epidermis.
scenes.narration: Repressor stays high in both. Neither becomes neural, and the cluster gives no precursor.

scenes.tts: A double negative between neighbours acts as positive feedback. A small lead can grow.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: two inhibitions make positive feedback.
scenes.narration: A double negative between neighbours acts as positive feedback. A small lead can grow.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
